text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- President Le Duc Anh on Wednesday warned that growing individualism was slowing development, whittling away at confidence in the Communist Party and the state and discouraging foreign investors.
-- The Danish Government pledged a loan of $15 million for a ferryboat construction project in south of Vietnam.
-- Vietnam exported more than 138,000 tonnes of coffee in the first quarter of 1997.
-- The Ministry of Trade expects the trade deficit to increase to $1.1 billion in the second quarter from $849 million in the first quarter.
-- The World Bank and Vietnam's State Bank were expected to sign a credit agreement worth $195.6 million for upgrading Vietnam's national highway.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van kiet told the National Assembly that the country has no other choice than to pursue rapid and sustainable development.
-- A serious fire destroyed 30 hectares of forest in the Mekong Delta last week.
-- The Government has set up a special board to take charge of construction of the country's new north-south express way.
